content.title: Steelers shut down Joe Greene death hoax
content.text: Steelers confirm Greene is alive The Pittsburgh Steelers told outlets including TMZ and PEOPLE that rumors of Joe Greene’s death were “not accurate.” NFL reporter John McClain also confirmed after speaking with Greene’s family that the four-time Super Bowl champion is “doing great.” Greene, 79, spent his entire 13-year career with the Steelers, cementing his place as one of the franchise’s most iconic figures. Yahoo Sports + 3 How the hoax went viral The false claim began with a post on X by user 'Johnny Cadillac,' which amassed over 620,000 views before being debunked. The user later claimed they were misled by bad information but did not delete the original post. The rumor’s spread was amplified by recent legitimate celebrity death news, causing confusion and emotional reactions from fans. People + 2 Family and team push back on misinformation Greene’s family directly confirmed to reporters that he is alive, while the Steelers swiftly addressed and refuted the false reports. The original poster issued an apology citing poor research but left the post online. This incident highlights the role of official and family statements in quickly quelling harmful rumors about public figures. Yahoo Sports + 2 Greene’s legacy in NFL history As the last surviving member of the Steel Curtain defense, Greene’s career includes 10 Pro Bowls, two Defensive Player of the Year awards, and four Super Bowl titles. The Steelers retired his No. 75 jersey in 2014, and he was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1987. His dominance on the field and leadership off it have made him a benchmark for defensive excellence in the NFL. Pittsburgh Steelers On SI + 3 Death hoaxes and the digital age Greene’s case is part of a recurring pattern where false death reports of famous individuals spread rapidly online. Similar hoaxes have targeted other celebrities, exploiting the speed and reach of social media. The incident underscores the importance of verifying information before sharing, especially in the wake of genuine high-profile deaths. Sporting News 7 references
